tasks.title: Degrees to a CLI integer
tasks.solution: Coordinates in INAV are degrees × 10⁷ as an integer: pad the fractional part with zeros to seven digits and remove the point. 50.001260° → 500012600. Six digits without padding give a number ten times smaller — a point at 5° of latitude instead of 50°.

tasks.title: Longitude offset in meters
tasks.solution: E = Δlon × 1.113195 cm × cos(latitude). At 50° one unit is 0.716 cm: 42000 units give 300.5 m. Without the cosine you get the distance along latitude, which at 50° is 1.56 times larger.

tasks.title: A circular zone: inside or outside
tasks.solution: For a circle vertex 1 holds the radius in centimeters: r/100 meters. N = a × 0.01113195 m, E = b × 0.01113195 × 0.64279 m, the distance to the center is √(N² + E²). Margin = radius − distance; the aircraft is inside while the distance is strictly less than the radius (and the altitude is within the range of the zone).

tasks.title: Autoland glide slope
tasks.solution: h_fa = approach alt / 3 × 2 in integers (5000 gives 3332). The final leg goes from h_fa to −h_fa and reaches the target when 10 % of 2L is left: tan γ = 2 × h_fa / (1.8 × L). For 5000 and 40000 — 5.29°. The answer atan(h_fa / L) understates the angle by a factor of 1.11.

tasks.title: Where the motor is cut
tasks.solution: The slope k = 2 × h_fa / (1.8 × L). From WP_FINAL_APPROACH to the glide altitude: (h_fa − g) / k. What is left to the safehome is L − (h_fa − g) / k = L × (0.1 + 0.9 × g / h_fa). For 5000, 40000 and 200: 400 × (0.1 + 0.054) = 61.6 m.

tasks.title: Tailwind component
tasks.solution: The headwind component = V × cos(the “from” direction − the heading), and the tailwind component is the same with the opposite sign. Wind from 120°, heading 270°: −V × cos(−150°) = +0.87 V. INAV compares with nav_fw_land_max_tailwind not this component but the full wind speed: below the threshold the wind is simply ignored.
